strength: Clean, fast, fair 2-player push-your-luck loop with unambiguous rules, balanced seats (gap 1.2), and trivial production cost.
weakness: The bait hurdle is inert (claimed 99% of the time), so 'leave lowest' is still correct and the game's only differentiator from Port Royal and Flip 7 does not show in play. Runaway leader is 74.8% against a 65% target.
required_changes: Make the bait hurdle bind (claim needs pile >= 2x bait, or a failed claimer pays a pile card). Target: smart leaver deviates from leave-lowest in 25%+ of choices, with leave-lowest and leave-highest both under 60%.
Runaway leader: accept and document 74.8%, or test one catch-up rule (trailing player claims bait on pile >= bait). Target: halfway leader at 65% or less, seat gap 5 or less.
Delete stale design notes (unchecked-originality line, considered-but-not-adopted paragraph) so panel readers do not copy them.
Before any physical prototype, do a plain web check for existing leave-one-card-as-bait games; the pitch must not call the shared river new.
revision_reason: Yes, narrowly: the hurdle fix is a clear one-line testable change aimed at the only differentiator, but if it fails, park or pitch as a plain filler.
